scope.fixture: synthetic grayscale SOF0 baseline JPEG fixtures; full-frame outputs are compared byte-for-byte with pinned jpeg-js 0.4.4
huffmanPrefixCoverage: canonical code lengths 1–6 are decoded through the lookup path after a warmup block leaves six buffered bits; each case checks that only the actual code length is consumed

63 six-bit prefixes 000000–111110 are exercised with seven buffered bits and alternating DC categories; AC codes of one or two bits keep the next lookup aligned, and output pixels are compared with jpeg-js
the remaining six-bit prefix 111111 misses the table and valid seven-bit code 1111110 succeeds through bitwise fallback
the seven-bit all-ones code 1111111 remains invalid after the six-bit lookup miss
AC decoding with zero through five buffered bits uses bitwise fallback
existing stuffed FF00 entropy, restart-marker RST0–RST7, restart padding, malformed input, and JPEG pixel-oracle regressions remain in the targeted suite

confirmed: the warmed entropy-reader bit counts exercise the six-bit lookup for canonical lengths 1–6 and prefixes 000000–111110
prefix 111111 misses the table and the valid 1111110 code falls back without cross-byte peeking

independentReview.limitation: The pixel regression does not independently prove that every runtime decode took the lookup fast path; a completely empty lookup would preserve semantics through the bitwise fallback. Static path accounting confirms the intended states, and alternating symbols detect incorrect neighboring-entry mappings.

limitations: Synthetic grayscale cases and the pinned jpeg-js comparison are a narrow regression reference, not an independent JPEG correctness oracle or broad corpus evaluation.
This unit result does not establish 4:2:0 color fidelity, memory limits, ASAR/package behavior, the 3000 ms product deadline, or complete T04 acceptance.
